_why: Three UI rules fire here, and all three assume a Control Panel addon. This one has no Control
Panel surface at all: no CP page, no fieldtype, no widget, no nav item. Everything it ships runs
on the public frontend of a site, which is the case none of these rules was written for.
ui.statamic-cms-package expects a package.json to mean a CP Vite build, and asks for @statamic/cms
in devDependencies so the UI kit is pinned to the Statamic version in vendor/. Nothing here imports
from @statamic/cms/ui, and adding the dependency would pull in a UI kit nothing uses. The
package.json exists for esbuild, Tiptap and playwright-core.
ui.vite-config wants a vite.config.js because resources/js exists. There is no CP bundle to build.
The one bundled file, resources/dist/inline-edit-rich.js, is built by scripts/build-rich.mjs with
esbuild into a plain IIFE that a <script> tag on a client's page can load, which is not something
Statamic's Vite setup produces. The build is committed and CI rebuilds it and fails on a diff, so
the guarantee the rule is really after — the shipped bundle matches its source — is kept, just not
by Vite.
ui.no-dom-piercing flags document.body.appendChild in rich.js. That rule protects a Vue component
tree in the CP. The element in question is the toolbar that appears over a text selection on a
client's own page, and it has to be a direct child of body and position: fixed: anywhere else, the
first ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it, and on a real client site that ancestor exists.
Revisit all three the day this addon grows a real CP screen. Then the rules are right and these
entries are wrong.
release.editions is an INFO, not a rule, and it asks a question rather than reporting a fault:
"Confirm this is a single-edition commercial addon." Confirmed on 2026-09-19 — one product, no
Core/Pro split, sold inside the suite. The field stays absent because the linter is right that a
declared edition without a feature behind it cannot gate anything.
